hero.lead: A nation of 836,000 with forest across almost nine tenths of its land, where oil output is rising, the IMF projects growth of 22.3% this year and the Natural Resource Fund held $3.3 billion at the end of 2025.

capital.heading: Oil wealth saved in a fund, to be spent on what lasts.

register.name: Natural Resource Fund transfer to Budget 2026
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · Budget Speech of 26 January 2026 · G$495bn, about US$2.374bn · in a budget of G$1.558 trillion
register.note: US$2.463 billion was withdrawn from the Fund to finance Budget 2025
register.text: The Government estimates the transfer from the Natural Resource Fund to the national budget at G$495 billion for 2026, about US$2.374 billion, in a budget of G$1.558 trillion. The Fund held US$3.250 billion at the end of 2025, net of withdrawals. The budget allots G$183.6 billion to education, G$161.1 billion to health and G$159.1 billion to housing in 2026.

register.name: Guyana One Health Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) and the Pandemic Fund · Approved 26 March 2025 · IDA credit US$7M · Pandemic Fund grant US$15M
register.note: Laboratories, digital disease surveillance and veterinary and wildlife diagnostics
register.text: A US$22 million project, a US$7 million credit from the World Bank’s International Development Association and a US$15 million grant from the Pandemic Fund, to strengthen health resilience. It upgrades and decentralises the laboratory network, including the National Public Health Reference Laboratory, moves health surveillance from paper to digital platforms and expands veterinary and wildlife diagnostics. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Integrated Transport Corridors Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Approved 27 February 2025 · signed at the Annual Meetings, 13 to 18 October 2025
register.note: Drainage, slope stabilisation, embankments and road safety on low-lying roads
register.text: A US$156 million project, funded through the World Bank’s International Development Association, to upgrade and rehabilitate roads so that they better withstand natural hazards and are safer to use, with drainage, slope stabilisation, embankments, non-motorised lanes and mobility plans for women and other vulnerable groups. Most of the network lies on low-lying coastal plains exposed to rising seas, heavier rainfall and flooding. It serves livelihood, by keeping people connected to work, markets and services.

register.name: Coastal Adaptation and Resilience
register.detail: World Bank · P503393 · Approved, press release of 10 June 2024 · financed by the Guyana REDD+ Investment Fund
register.note: More than 45 drainage assets, mainly sluices, for about 320,000 people
register.text: A US$45 million World Bank project financed by the Guyana REDD+ Investment Fund (GRIF), a financial intermediary fund; the World Bank recalls that Norway pays Guyana for reducing emissions from deforestation and that these payments fund the Low Carbon Development Strategy. It repairs or replaces more than 45 drainage infrastructure assets, mainly sluices, for around 320,000 people, about 40 percent of the population. It protects homes and farms on the low-lying coast.

register.name: Enhancing Policies for Human Capital Accumulation
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · P180216 · development policy financing · SDR 26.7M in a single tranche · signed 15 December 2023 · closing date 31 December 2024
register.note: Principal repayable in instalments from June 2030 to December 2035
register.text: A single-tranche development policy credit of SDR 26.7 million (about US$35 million) from the World Bank’s International Development Association, treated as non-concessional financing. It supported education reforms: school resource allocation, textbooks, teacher policy, school facilities, learning assessment, education data and technical and vocational training. Its closing date, 31 December 2024, has passed.

register.name: Second Environmental Sector Policy-Based Loan
register.detail: CDB · Approved 2 April 2026 · Ordinary Capital Resources · second of a US$175M two-loan programme
register.note: Reforms in biodiversity management, climate resilience and water governance
register.text: A US$50 million policy-based loan from the Caribbean Development Bank, the second of a US$175 million two-loan programme, for reforms in biodiversity management, climate resilience and water governance. The Bank cites the restoration of carbon-storing ecosystems, early-warning systems for public health and water supply systems for coastal communities. It serves the water standard.

register.name: Environmental Sector Policy-Based Loan (first loan)
register.detail: CDB · US$125M disbursed in July 2025 · first of a US$175M two-loan programme
register.note: The first part of the programme that the loan of April 2026 completes
register.text: The first loan of the Caribbean Development Bank’s US$175 million two-loan environmental programme for Guyana, disbursed as US$125 million in July 2025. The programme supports Guyana’s response to climate change and its management of natural resources. It serves the water standard and the protection of the coast.

register.name: Water and Sanitation Conditional Credit Line (CCLIP)
register.detail: IDB · approval reported 23 July 2025 · credit line of US$30M; first loan US$15.57M · 25 years, 5.5 years’ grace, SOFR-based · co-financed by JICA (US$36.33M)
register.note: A new water treatment plant at Diamond, East Bank Demerara, for about 151,560 people
register.text: A US$30 million IDB conditional credit line for investment projects, whose first loan of US$15.57 million is co-financed by JICA, to make drinking water and sewerage services more resilient, reliable and sustainable. The main works are a new water treatment plant at Diamond, East Bank Demerara, transmission pipelines, the reduction of non-revenue water and digital upgrades, for about 151,560 people. It serves the water standard.

register.name: Support to Human Services in Guyana II
register.detail: IDB · GY-L1089 · Approved 29 May 2025 · policy-based · 20 years, 5.5 years’ grace, SOFR-based · closed
register.note: The second and final operation of a programmatic series for the social safety net
register.text: A US$350 million IDB policy-based loan, the second and final operation of a programmatic series, for the social safety net run by the Ministry of Human Services and Social Security: the digitisation of services, the senior citizens’ pension programme, which covers more than 82,000 people, and public assistance for persons with disabilities, which has reached more than 6,000 people. The IDB lists the operation as closed. It serves livelihood.

register.name: Health Care Network Strengthening in Guyana
register.detail: IDB · GY-L1080 · Approved 7 December 2022 · investment loan 5706/OC-GY · 25 years, 5.5 years’ grace, SOFR-based
register.note: Seven hospitals, four of them in the hinterland, for about 406,000 people
register.text: A US$97 million IDB investment loan to strengthen the health care network: it expands seven hospitals, four of them in the hinterland in Regions 1, 7, 8 and 9, with Linden Hospital, New Amsterdam Hospital and Georgetown Public Hospital, adds telehealth in more than 15 facilities and improves supply chains, maternal and child health and pandemic preparedness, for about 406,000 people. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Water Supply Improvement Project
register.detail: JICA · Signed 22 January 2026, Georgetown · ODA loan of up to ¥5,242M · 1.9% · repayment 15 years, grace 5 years · co-financed with the IDB (US$15.57M)
register.note: The first Japanese ODA loan agreement with Guyana
register.text: The first Japanese ODA loan agreement with Guyana, of up to 5,242 million yen, co-financed with the IDB, for a new water treatment plant with pipelines and for measures against non-revenue water in Demerara-Mahaica: network renewal, leak repair and ultrasonic smart water meters. It serves the water standard.

register.name: Gas-to-Energy Project
register.detail: Export-Import Bank of the United States · Board approval announced 26 December 2024 · to the Ministry of Finance
register.note: A 300 MW combined cycle power plant and a natural gas separation plant
register.text: A US$527 million loan from the Export-Import Bank of the United States to the Ministry of Finance for a natural gas separation plant, a 300 MW combined cycle gas turbine power plant and services for the gas supply pipeline near Georgetown. EXIM says the project will double installed electric capacity and reduce carbon dioxide emissions by more than 460,000 tonnes a year. It serves the energy standard.
by: Export-Import Bank of the United States

register.name: Institute of Private Enterprise Development (IPED)
register.detail: IDB Invest · Announced 15 January 2026 · two tranches of US$2.5M, from IDB Invest and from the JICA TADAC Fund
register.note: Credit for micro and small enterprises, with a focus on women, young people and rural entrepreneurs
register.text: A US$5 million loan to IPED, Guyana’s leading non-bank financial institution, in two equal tranches of US$2.5 million from IDB Invest and from the JICA Trust Fund Achieving Development of Latin America and the Caribbean (TADAC Fund), administered by the IDB. It widens credit for micro and small enterprises, with a focus on women, young people and rural entrepreneurs. It serves livelihood.

register.name: Sale of ART-TREES carbon credits to Hess Corporation
register.detail: Hess Corporation · Signed 2 December 2022 · 37.5 million credits, 2016 to 2030 · at least US$750M over a decade · minimum prices of US$15 to US$25 a credit
register.note: 15% of revenues for village-led plans in Indigenous villages and communities
register.text: An agreement under which Hess Corporation is committed to buy 37.5 million forest carbon credits issued under the ART-TREES standard: 12.5 million for 2016 to 2020 and 2.5 million a year for 2021 to 2030, at minimum prices rising from US$15 to US$25 a credit, for at least US$750 million over the coming decade. Fifteen percent of the revenues are dedicated to village-led plans for Indigenous villages and communities. It pays the nation for keeping its forest standing.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Oil and Gas
items.label: Of GDP from oil and gas rents, 2021
items.text: Oil and gas already earn; the task is to turn the rent into assets that outlast it.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Minerals
items.label: Of GDP from mineral rents, 2021
items.text: Metals and minerals already earn; the task is to keep more of their value at home.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 28.9% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: Institute of Private Enterprise Development (IPED)
items.text: A non-bank lender established in 1986 that finances, trains and advises micro, small and growing businesses; it has made more than 140,000 loans to entrepreneurs in four decades, sustains more than 10,000 jobs a year and in January 2026 took a US$5 million loan from IDB Invest and the JICA TADAC Fund to lend more to women, young people and rural entrepreneurs.

items.name: Iwokrama International Centre
items.text: A centre for rain forest conservation and development in central Guyana that earns its own income from sustainable tourism (US$537,892 in 2025) and sustainable forestry (US$350,475 in 2025) and trains people from partner communities such as Fair View, Surama, Apoteri and Rewa; its Wildlife Clubs reached more than 400 young people in 18 communities in 2025.

items.name: Guyana Responsible Parenthood Association (GRPA)
items.text: An association registered in 1975 that describes itself as the leading provider of sexual and reproductive health services in Guyana, offering family planning, HIV testing and treatment, cancer screening, laboratory and diagnostic testing and adolescent-friendly care, which it describes as affordable, from its clinic on Quamina Street, Georgetown; in 2026 it introduced the contraceptive patch in Guyana.

items.name: Surama Eco-Lodge
items.text: A tourism business developed, owned and managed by Surama, an Indigenous Makushi village, and described as the first community-owned and run tourism project in Guyana: villagers work as cooks, cleaners, drivers and guides, staff are hired on rotation to spread the work, and local farmers and fishers supply the food.

items.name: Caiman House Field Station
items.text: A non-profit field station in the Indigenous village of Yupukari, set up to study the black caiman and now run entirely by community members; guests stay at the station, join the caiman research and visit the village’s sustainable furniture-making ventures, and their spending goes to locally driven initiatives.
